summary.lead: Perch gives the people who run an independent hotel the calm of knowing every room is handled, without turning the hotel into a control room.
essence: For owner-managers of 20 to 80 room hotels who run housekeeping and maintenance on paper and a group chat.
It should feel like a well-kept ledger: quiet, exact, on the side of the staff.
Competent without being corporate, warm without being cute, and never a dashboard that watches people.
It must work as a 16 px app icon on a housekeeper's phone and embroidered in one colour on a uniform.

product.value: A phone app and a front-desk screen that tell every member of a hotel's staff which rooms and repairs are theirs today, and tell the manager what is done.

reason.value: Independent hotels lose rooms and reviews to things nobody was told about: a broken shower reported on paper, a late checkout that never reached housekeeping.
reason.quote: Nobody is lazy in a hotel. Things fall between two people, that's all.

problem.value: The tools sold to hotels are built for chains: long set-up, a manager's dashboard first, staff treated as rows.

instead_of.value: A paper list at reception and a WhatsApp group. The paper is faster to write and everyone already knows how.
instead_of.quote: The paper never needs a login.

difference.value: Built for the housekeeper's first minute, not the manager's first report: a new member of staff uses it without training.

proof.value: No structural reason to believe yet. Two pilot hotels onboarded their teams in a morning, which is an anecdote, not a proof.

audiences.name: Owner-managers of independent hotels
audiences.who: 20 to 80 rooms, often family-run, the manager also covers reception.
audiences.need: To stop being the only memory of the building.
audiences.quote: I want to be able to leave at six without my phone ringing at seven.

audiences.name: Housekeeping and maintenance staff
audiences.who: Often not native English speakers, on their own phones.
audiences.need: To know what is theirs today without being watched.

frame_inherited.value: Hotel management software, next to property management systems.

frame_wanted.value: The hotel's own logbook, next to the paper it replaces.

territories.name: The well-kept ledger
territories.description: Quiet and exact. The hotel's own book, kept properly.

territories.name: The colleague who never forgets
territories.description: Warm and close to the staff. Makes the day lighter.
territories.keep: on the side of the staff, speaks plainly

territories.name: The control tower
territories.description: Everything visible at once. The manager sees all.
territories.reason: It is what the staff fear, and what every competitor sells.

territories.name: The modern challenger
territories.description: Bold, shakes up old hotel software.

promise.value: Nothing in the building falls between two people.

horizon.value: In five years, the default for independent hotels in the UK and Ireland, then French and Italian family hotels.

scale.value: A product company of thirty people, not a platform.

must_carry.value: The brand has to survive translation into French and Italian and a second product for small restaurants.

values.value: The staff are users, never the thing being measured.
values.instance: Turned down a pilot with a 400-room group that wanted per-housekeeper timing reports.
values.quote: They wanted a stopwatch. I said no and it cost us the quarter.

values.instance: Removed a feature two hotels had asked for because it needed a ten-minute explanation.

traits.more_than: more a head housekeeper than a consultant
more a note left on the desk than a notification

dimensions.name: Tone
dimensions.orientation: Plain and exact, with dry warmth.
dimensions.boundary: Warm but never cute: no mascot, no jokes in the interface.

evidence.signal: fits: Muji, Monocle; too plain: Mews; too playful: Mailchimp, Duolingo
"No training, ever": words must explain themselves
fits: Monocle, Muji; too quiet: Linear; too loud: Stripe

dimensions.name: People in the picture
dimensions.orientation: The building and its objects rather than faces.
dimensions.contradictions: Refused every portrait of staff, yet wants to be on their side.

evidence.signal: none of the brands shown fits (leans between); too faces: Belmond

tensions.crossed_when: A screen could belong to a bank, or a sentence could not be said aloud at the front desk.
The work is not recognisable once the logo is covered.

think.value: These people have worked in a hotel.
think.quote: I want them to think: these people have carried linen.

feel.value: Relief, then quiet pride in a building that runs well.

references.hypothesis: Does the founder want to be read as hotel software at all?

references.name: Mailchimp
references.hypothesis: How much humour can a work tool carry?

references.name: Monocle
references.why: Read by hotel owners; print discipline as a sign of care.
references.hypothesis: Does print craft read as serious or as nostalgic?
copy: Keeping an eye and an ear on the world

references.name: Stripe
references.why: The reference for a trusted tool.

references.name: Linear
references.why: A task tool people love using.
references.hypothesis: Is sobriety liked for its look or for the sense of control?

references.why: Used daily by people who are not native speakers, like much of the staff.

references.name: Belmond

signals.statement: Print discipline: rules, small labels, real tables.
No mascot and no illustrated characters.
No dashboard as the first image of the brand.
A wordmark that can be embroidered in one colour.
Photography of the building and its objects rather than of people.

founder_vs_audience.wish: The founder is drawn to very quiet, print-like references.
founder_vs_audience.risk: Housekeeping staff on a small phone need large, obvious controls; a magazine's restraint can read as hard to use.
founder_vs_audience.arbitration: Quiet on the brand's surfaces, generous and plain in the product. Decided by the founder.

principles.principle: If it needs explaining, it is not finished.
principles.because: No training is a value the founder has paid for.

principles.principle: Show the building, not the dashboard.
principles.because: The dashboard is the category's first image and what the staff fear.

principles.principle: Say it the way it would be said at the front desk.
principles.because: Plain speech was chosen every time it was offered.

items.constraint: Works in English, French and Italian; no wordplay in the mark.
Staff use their own phones, many of them old Android devices.
No trademark search has been done on the name in the EU.

constraints.timeline: Identity needed before the spring trade fair, in about ten weeks.

logo_contexts.context: App icon on a phone home screen
logo_contexts.note: The product is a phone app for staff: must read at 16 px beside other work apps.
The product has a front-desk screen.
Two pilot hotels asked for it.

logo_contexts.context: Printed door hangers and room cards

evaluation.criterion: Reads at 16 px and in one colour.
A housekeeper would not feel it is the manager's tool.
Could not be mistaken for Mews or Cloudbeds with the logo covered.

interactions.question: What happened the last time something went wrong in one of your hotels?
interactions.answer: A shower reported on paper on Friday, found by a guest on Sunday.

interactions.question: What do they use today instead, and what does it do better?
interactions.answer: Paper and WhatsApp. No login, everyone knows how.

interactions.question: When a hotel picks you over Mews, what is the sentence they say?
interactions.answer: My team used it the first morning.

interactions.question: If you lost one of these tomorrow, which would end the company?
Which is closest, which goes, what do you keep from a second?
interactions.answer: The ledger. Drop the control tower. Keep 'on the side of the staff' from the colleague.

interactions.question: Tell me about the last time you turned down money.
interactions.answer: The 400-room group that wanted timing reports.

interactions.question: In five years, which is closest?
options: The default for independents in a few countries
Sold to a large hotel-software company
interactions.answer: The default for independents in a few countries

interactions.question: The manager closes the app at six. They feel like after...

a good session at the gym
ticking the last box of a tax form

open_questions.why: The founder's taste, untested on buyers.

Will the logo be printed on door hangers and room cards?

limits: Everything here is the founder's account. No customer was interviewed.
The references are a sample of nine brands from the hotel world and from tools that solved a similar problem, one of which could not be captured. They show taste, not the market.
No structural reason to believe was found for the difference.

hypotheses: The category opens on a dashboard and a blue or purple gradient.
No competitor addresses the staff rather than the manager.

settled: Type and rules carry the character, not colour
open: How distinctive the one strange element may be
refusals: A dashboard as the first image
